item.text:
# Félix Tshisekedi in 2024: 1B.6 research note

## Bottom line
I found **no evidence of nuclear proliferation** by allies, proxies, clients, or domestic factions in the DRC case. The relevant 2024 record is instead about **armed proxies and disarmament**, especially the Wazalendo militias and the P-DDRCS program.

The evidence is **mixed**:
- **Positive:** Tshisekedi publicly pushed disarmament/demobilization and reportedly instructed Wazalendo to be brought in line.
- **Negative:** Reuters reporting shows his government also relied on proxies and militias in the east, with weak control and sanctions concerns.

So the best-supported reading is: **some resistance to uncontrolled proxy militarization, but not consistent or clean resistance to proliferation when short-term security interests were at stake.**

## Accepted claims

- [**Programme de désarmement et démobilisation : une alternative pour la paix et la cohésion sociale**](https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-demobilisation-une-alternative-pour-la-paix-et-la-cohesion-sociale/)  
  - **Publisher:** ACP  
  - **Date:** 2024-03-22  
  - **Claim-level summary:** The government described P-DDRCS as a national stabilization, peace, and cohesion program that also aims to restore state authority where it was absent. This is direct evidence of a disarmament-and-demobilization posture, which supports resistance to factional weapons proliferation.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.6, 1B.4, 1B.1

- [**Programme de désarmement et relèvement communautaire: nomination d'une nouvelle équipe de coordination nationale**](https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-relevement-communautaire-nomination-dune-nouvelle-equipe-de-coordination-nationale/)  
  - **Publisher:** ACP  
  - **Date:** 2024-12-20  
  - **Claim-level summary:** The presidency appointed a new national coordination team for the disarmament, demobilization, community recovery, and stabilization program. That suggests Tshisekedi was still trying to operationalize disarmament and control over armed actors late in 2024.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.6, 1B.4, 1B.3

- [**Army disarray hobbles Congo's fight with Rwanda-backed rebels, officers say**](https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2024-07-17  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that the government relied on a loose alliance of pro-government militias known as Wazalendo, that the army had no control over them, and that they were often poorly trained and undisciplined. The same report says a provincial military governor said Tshisekedi instructed that Wazalendo be brought in line. This is the clearest mixed evidence: he tried to discipline proxies, but his coalition still depended on them.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.6, 1B.3, 1B.1

- [**Congo army retreat from Bukavu leads to clashes with allied militias**](https://theprint.in/world/congo-army-retreat-from-bukavu-leads-to-clashes-with-allied-militias/2500519/)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2025-02-17, describing the 2025 collapse with 2024 context  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters described Wazalendo as allied militias that were recruiting, disarming retreating soldiers, and operating with little cohesion. This is negative contextual evidence that the proxy structure Tshisekedi tolerated had dangerous spillover effects and poor command discipline.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.6, 1B.3

- [**Democratic Republic of Congo army says it thwarted attempted coup**](https://www.tbsnews.net/worldbiz/africa/democratic-republic-congo-army-says-it-thwarted-attempted-coup-855206)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** 2024-05-19  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Armed men, including foreigners, attacked the presidency complex and briefly occupied part of the seat of power before security forces retook control. This is not nuclear proliferation evidence, but it is negative evidence that the security environment around Tshisekedi was unstable and vulnerable to armed factional action.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.6, 1B.3

- [**Face à la presse, le Président Félix Tshisekedi a peint un tableau d’espoir de la RDC**](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/face_a_la_presse_le_president_felix_tshisekedi_a_peint_un_tableau_despoir_de_la_rdc)  
  - **Publisher:** Présidence RDC  
  - **Date:** 2024-02-23  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Tshisekedi said the army was undergoing a major buildup and that he wanted a definitive peace. This is supportive only in a limited sense: it shows a desire to restore state control, but it also shows reliance on militarization rather than a clean break from armed coercion.  
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.6, 1B.3, 1B.1

## Search gap

- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that Tshisekedi had or enabled any **nuclear** proliferation network.
- I also found **no evidence** of him resisting nuclear proliferation by allies or domestic factions, because there was no visible nuclear proliferation issue to resist.
- The real-world analogue in the DRC record is **conventional proxy militarization**: Tshisekedi publicly supported disarmament programs, but his government also depended on proxy militias like Wazalendo.

## Best-supported judgment
- **Strict nuclear reading:** not applicable; no evidence of nuclear proliferation activity.
- **Broader proxy-militarization reading:** mixed. Tshisekedi showed some resistance through disarmament and command discipline, but he also tolerated and operationally relied on armed proxies.
